coverage_limits: OpenAlex's anonymous daily budget (shared by every agent on this IP) ran out after three query passes, so the remaining journal sweeps used full Crossref listings, which carry no abstracts for Elsevier titles (Thinking Skills and Creativity, CHB, Acta Psychologica, Journal of Creativity) and few for APA and Wiley titles. For those items, design, N and results come from ScienceDirect search snippets or are left null, and three items (Li et al. 2026 and Li 2026 in PACA; Yao 2026 in TSC) are included on title alone. Publisher pages (ScienceDirect, Wiley, APA PsycNet, eScholarship) returned 403 to scripts, so no full texts were read except one working-paper PDF. The arXiv API was rate-limited for part of the run, so only four psychology-oriented arXiv queries ran; arXiv is mainly other lanes' territory. OSF title filters see titles only, so PsyArXiv preprints whose titles lack the filter terms can be missed. Scientific Reports was not listed in full. Several included records are borderline (self-reported creativity outcomes, an AI evaluator rather than a generator, process studies without a no-AI arm, AI-only model comparisons with small human benchmarks); each is flagged in its evidence field.

candidates.title: “Who” Is the Best Creative Thinking Partner? An Experimental Investigation of Human–Human, Human–Internet, and Human– AI Co‐Creation
candidates.venue: The Journal of Creative Behavior 59(3), e1519
candidates.task: alternate uses, consequences and problem-solving tasks with a partner
candidates.evidence: Between-group experiment with four conditions (human-human dyads, human-internet, and two human-ChatGPT groups with basic or specific instructions); human-rated creativity on divergent-thinking tasks was highest in human-human dyads, with no group differences on problem solving. Random assignment is not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Generative AI as an External Cognitive Tool for Developing Creative Intelligence in Visual Design: A Mixed-Methods Randomized Study Using Cognitive Load Indicators and Motivational Modeling
candidates.evidence: Six-week randomized instructional experiment comparing GenAI-integrated instruction with traditional instruction; blind expert ratings of domain-specific creative performance were higher with GenAI.

candidates.title: Human vs. LLM Creativity: A Comparative Analysis of Task-Dependent Asymmetry and Linguistic Mechanisms
candidates.evidence: Two-stage design comparing Human-Only, LLM-Only and LLM-Assisted writing; humans showed higher originality on high-demand creative tasks, and LLM-assisted writing did not beat LLM-only output ("collaboration trap", anchoring). Assignment procedure and N not given in the abstract.

candidates.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Preservice Science Teachers’ Analogical Reasoning: Evidence from Analogy Design
candidates.task: analogy design by preservice science teachers
candidates.evidence: Preservice teachers designed analogies with AI (n = 62) or without AI (n = 71); AI-supported analogies differed in format, semantic distance, and richness. Assignment method not stated; outcomes are coded product features rather than creativity ratings.

candidates.title: Unlocking creativity with artificial intelligence (AI): Field and experimental evidence on the Goldilocks (curvilinear) effect of human–AI collaboration
candidates.task: entrepreneurial challenge with ChatGPT; field survey of creative workers
candidates.evidence: Two experiments assigned 139 business professionals and 319 working adults to collaborate with ChatGPT to varying degrees; moderate collaboration produced the highest judge-rated creativity (curvilinear effect), replicated in a multiwave survey (N = 188). N is the total across studies; random assignment wording taken from search snippets, abstract only partly accessible.

candidates.title: EEG assessment of artificial intelligence-generated content impact on student creative performance and neurophysiological states in product design
candidates.evidence: Design students used AIGC tools (ChatGPT, Midjourney, Stable Diffusion) or traditional software; AIGC group had higher rated creative performance (d = 0.55) and higher EEG concentration. Allocation method not stated.

candidates.title: Effects of integrating a structured design thinking strategy into generative AI-supported design learning on students’ design achievement, creative self-efficacy, and problem-solving skills
candidates.evidence: Three conditions (GAI with structured design-thinking strategy, GAI without strategy, traditional learning); outcomes were design achievement, creative self-efficacy and problem solving, highest in GAI plus strategy. Included for recall: unclear whether design achievement is a creativity rating.

candidates.title: The influence of collaborative music creation supported by generative artificial intelligence on students’ creativity
candidates.task: collaborative music creation in university courses
candidates.evidence: Mixed-method study with experimental and control groups comparing GAI-supported collaborative music creation with conventional instruction; outcomes (creative interest, creative self-efficacy, perceived creative competence) appear to be self-reported, so it may fail the scored-output criterion.

candidates.title: Borrowed or kept? How self-generation-first and direct-adoption AI workflows shape immediate unaided reasoning
candidates.authors: Liu, Guo, Gao, Chen, Zhu, Chang
candidates.task: argumentative essay writing, then a parallel unaided essay
candidates.evidence: Three-arm randomized experiment (900 randomized, 659 analyzed): self-generation-first AI workflow, direct-adoption AI workflow, or no AI, then a second essay without AI 15-20 minutes later; blind raters scored reasoning quality, idea diversity and originality, and direct-adoption users reasoned worse unaided than never-AI participants.

candidates.title: Generative AI as a cognitive support tool in early-stage design ideation: A human–AI co-ideation experiment
candidates.evidence: Counterbalanced within-subjects experiment: design students did human-only brainstorming and a text-and-image AI-assisted workflow; experts rated AI-assisted outputs higher on problem framing but human-only outputs higher on innovation and solution strategies.

candidates.title: Sequential Human-AI Collaboration Impairs Narrative Creativity in University Students: A Randomized Controlled Trial
candidates.evidence: Randomized controlled experiment comparing AI-first, AI-follow, AI-parallel and human-only collaboration; human and AI raters scored narrative creativity, and sequential AI collaboration lowered creativity relative to human-only writing.

candidates.title: How and for whom using generative AI affects creativity: A field experiment
candidates.task: workplace creativity at a technology consulting firm
candidates.evidence: Field experiment randomly assigning employees to receive LLM assistance or not; supervisor and external evaluator ratings of employee creativity rose with LLM assistance, especially for employees high in metacognitive strategies. N not in the abstract.

candidates.title: Supporting Brainstorming with a Collaborative Platform or a Generative Artificial Intelligence Tool: An Exploratory Study
candidates.authors: Gerardini, Sarcinella, Borghesi, Pozzi, Gaggioli, Chirico
candidates.task: group brainstorming with DALL-E or a Miro whiteboard
candidates.evidence: 2x2 design (online vs offline; DALL-E vs Miro) with 16 groups of five; two raters scored fluency, elaboration, flexibility and originality of ideas, and online DALL-E sessions produced more elaborated ideas. Assignment method not stated.

candidates.title: Enhancing creative writing through AI-powered co-creation with cognitive and emotional outcomes
candidates.evidence: Three groups (high AI support, low AI support, conventional instruction) with pre- and post-tests of creative writing; both AI groups outperformed the control. Allocation method not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Cross-lingual effects of AI-generated content on human work
candidates.task: business email writing in English, Arabic and Chinese
candidates.evidence: Study 2 randomized 480 participants to write emails with or without AI-generated content; trained evaluators rated quality, and AI use was associated with less creative and less actionable output in Arabic and Chinese than in English.

candidates.title: Chat-GPT4 can Enhance Marketing Creativity. But Human Ego Can Hamper its Potential
other_versions: doi 10.2139/ssrn.5135496 (SSRN version, Gill and Hoxha, retitled "Chat-GPT4 Does Enhance Creativity. But Human Ego Can Hamper its Potential")
candidates.evidence: Study 1 compared ChatGPT-4 slogans with human slogans (higher novelty and quality but lower diversity); Study 2 found GenAI assistance raised slogan quality for less creative people but not for egocentric creators. Preregistered; N and assignment details not in the abstract.

candidates.title: Fostering children’s creativity through LLM-driven storytelling with a social robot
candidates.task: children's storytelling with a social robot
candidates.evidence: Children told stories with a robot driven by a fine-tuned LLM showing creative or non-creative behavior; fluency, flexibility, elaboration and originality were scored, and Study 1 (38 children) found no effect of robot creativity. N covers Study 1 only.

candidates.title: AI models as cultural beings: Investigating AI cultural biases and the impact of cultural alignment on human–AI creative collaboration
candidates.task: creative problem solving with ChatGPT or ErnieBot
candidates.evidence: Study 2 experiment varied cultural alignment between users and AI models; aligned pairs produced more useful but not more novel solutions on local tasks, replicated in a field dyad study. N not in the abstract.

candidates.title: The Double-Edged Sword of Creative Control in Designer-AI Co-Creation with Design Experience as a Boundary Condition
candidates.evidence: Between-subjects scenario experiment varying creative control in designer-AI co-creation; design creativity rose via psychological ownership and fell via cognitive load. Included for recall: unclear whether creativity is rated on output or self-reported.

candidates.title: The value of generative AI in creative teams depends on when it enters collective search
candidates.evidence: 148 three-person teams were randomized to AI access during divergent search only, convergent selection only, the whole process, or not at all; AI during divergent search (and full access) raised human-rated creativity, while convergent-only access did not.

candidates.title: Human direction drives creativity with large language models
candidates.task: brainstorming and writing with ChatGPT or Gemini
candidates.evidence: Two experiments with ChatGPT (N = 234, 205) and a preregistered Gemini replication (N = 157), plus 6,290 naturalistic chats; people who directed rather than delegated produced more original content and less semantically similar ideas across the group. Creative direction is measured, not assigned.

candidates.title: Generative AI Does Not Erase Individual Differences in Human Creativity
candidates.task: idea generation and story writing with GPT-4o
candidates.evidence: Two studies measured creativity without AI and then with GPT-4o assistance; baseline creative ability and intelligence predicted the originality of AI-assisted stories and ideas. No randomized no-AI arm; included because it scores creativity of AI-assisted output.

candidates.title: Evaluating AI’s Ideas: The Role of Individual Creativity and Expertise in Human-AI Co-Creativity
candidates.task: engineering design problem with pre-generated GPT-3.5 ideas
candidates.evidence: Engineering (N = 99) and psychology (N = 212) students wrote a solution, evaluated GPT-3.5 ideas, and revised; originality and effectiveness of revised solutions improved in both groups. Within-person before/after exposure, no separate control.

candidates.title: Perspective taking shapes creative performance in human-AI collaboration
candidates.authors: Zhang, Peng, Wang, Hu, Chen, Zhao
candidates.task: alternative uses and product improvement tasks in dyads
candidates.evidence: Compared human-human and human-AI collaboration; human-AI dyads produced higher mean idea novelty on both tasks, and perspective-taking related differently to fluency, flexibility and novelty across collaboration types. N and assignment not given in the preprint abstract.

candidates.title: Hybrid Human–AI Societies Balance Creativity and Diversity
other_versions: OSF data project https://osf.io/ku9cj/ (doi 10.17605/osf.io/ku9cj; reports 1,473 humans and 8,590 AI agents)
candidates.task: iterated story transmission in social networks
candidates.evidence: Large network experiments with 1,363 humans and 7,865 AI bots compared human-only, AI-only and hybrid networks; hybrid networks combined high story creativity with the highest collective diversity, and humans in hybrid networks became more diverse than in human-only networks.

candidates.title: Scaffolding Creativity or Homogenizing Outputs?: GPT-based Virtual TA’s Impact on Student Ideation in Graduate Education
candidates.task: graduate course ideation on educational uses of a video game
candidates.evidence: Compared a 2023 cohort without and a 2024 cohort with JeepyTA, a GPT-powered teaching assistant; JeepyTA increased fully formed ideas but AI-driven ideation showed creative homogeneity, while student-driven ideas were more unique.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence Enhances Human Creativity Through Real-Time Evaluative Feedback
candidates.authors: de Chantal, Beaty, Laverghetta, et al.
candidates.task: real-world problem solutions and visual sketches with AI feedback
candidates.evidence: Preregistered online experiment (N = 554) and museum field experiment (N = 36,198) gave real-time AI originality feedback on human ideas; feedback raised originality. Included for recall: the AI scores ideas rather than generating them.

candidates.title: Understanding Creativity in Human–AI Collaboration: How Cognitive Strategies and Student Profiles Relate to Students’ Creativity
candidates.task: idea generation with GenAI in a lab session
candidates.evidence: Observational lab study of undergraduates using GenAI; cognitive strategies (e.g., conceptual combination) were linked to more original ideas, and AI-reliant profiles produced higher-quality but not more original ideas. No no-AI condition.

candidates.title: Prompting for Creative Problem-Solving: A Process-Mining Study
other_versions: PsyArXiv 10.31234/osf.io/68fh4_v2 ("How Students Prompt ChatGPT for Creative Problem-Solving: Process Mining of Hybrid Human-AI Regulation")
candidates.task: complex creative problem solving with ChatGPT-3.5
candidates.evidence: Process-mining study of how students prompted ChatGPT; prompting with evaluation criteria, context and feedback was associated with higher quality, elaboration and originality. No no-AI comparison.

candidates.title: Comparing AIGC and traditional idea generation methods: Evaluating their impact on creativity in the product design ideation phase
candidates.authors: Lin, Jiang, Deng, Bian, Fang, Zhu
candidates.evidence: Compares AIGC-based and traditional idea generation methods on creativity in the product design ideation phase. A search summary (which mixed several sources) suggests AIGC did not consistently beat traditional methods and that AI image quality mattered; abstract not accessible to scripts, so design, N and results are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: Enhancing human computer collaboration in design process: How AI-generated content elevates students’ creativity
candidates.task: student design process with AI-generated content
candidates.evidence: Search snippets report that an AIGC-based design method improved relevance, novelty, elaboration and thoroughness of student creative outcomes. Abstract not accessible; design and N unconfirmed.

candidates.title: Augmentation or limitation? Generative AI’s influence on college students’ creative problem-solving
candidates.evidence: Compared students with and without ChatGPT support on creative problem-solving performance across testing stages (steeper gains with ChatGPT); mentor interviews flagged idea homogenization. Details from search snippet; abstract not accessible.

candidates.title: How does generative artificial intelligence impact student creativity?
candidates.task: alternate uses test in a college creativity course
candidates.evidence: Mixed-methods study measuring fluency, flexibility, elaboration and originality on the AUT to assess ChatGPT-3 effects on students; reports gains in fluency, flexibility and elaboration but negative effects on creative confidence. Comparison structure unconfirmed (snippet only).

candidates.title: When proximal collaboration with AI hinders innovation: The moderating role of idea originality and reliance on AI
candidates.task: idea selection and implementation by employees
candidates.evidence: Experiment with 221 employees: proximal human-AI collaboration reduced idea selection (moderated by idea originality) and idea implementation. Outcome is innovation behavior rather than rated creativity; included for recall.

candidates.title: Designing AI for team ideation: How content strategy and participation style affect creative performance through team emergent states
candidates.evidence: Mixed-design experiment varying AI content strategy (breadth-first vs depth-first) and participation style (active vs passive); breadth-first AI raised divergent performance and depth-first AI raised convergence and solution completeness.

candidates.title: The analysis of generative artificial intelligence technology for innovative thinking and strategies in animation teaching
candidates.evidence: Experimental vs control groups (GAI-supported vs conventional animation teaching) with pre/post tests; reported gains in learning outcomes and innovative thinking. Included for recall: creativity measurement unclear from the abstract.

candidates.title: The Application of Multimodal Generative AI in College English Creative Writing Instruction
candidates.evidence: Teaching experiment with writing samples and questionnaires on multimodal GenAI-supported creative writing; reports enhanced creative expression. Comparison group and N not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Exploring the use of generative text AI in design creativity inquiries
candidates.venue: Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humans 6, 100219
candidates.task: design creativity inquiries with text GenAI in a course
candidates.evidence: Students iterated on ideas with text-based GenAI and peers rated originality, practicality, surprise and relevance. No no-AI comparison; included for recall.

candidates.title: Beyond Cognitive Support: Social Interaction and Affective Experience in AI-Assisted Creative Thinking Among University Students
candidates.evidence: All students solved creative problems with GPT-4.0; SEM linked social interaction and affect during collaboration to convergent (not divergent) thinking scores. No no-AI comparison.

candidates.title: Exploring cognitive strategies in human-AI interaction: ChatGPT's role in creative tasks
candidates.task: function-first and form-first creative tasks with ChatGPT
candidates.evidence: Coded 591 turns of student dyads using ChatGPT examples; most ideas repeated ChatGPT ideas rather than combining or improving them. Process study without a no-AI condition; relevant to convergence on AI ideas.

candidates.title: Digital muses empowering artistic creativity: The impact of human–generative AI interaction on the creative experience
candidates.venue: Psychology of Aesthetics, Creativity, and the Arts
candidates.evidence: Title indicates a study of how human-GenAI interaction affects the creative experience in art; abstract not accessible to API or search, so design and outcomes are unconfirmed. Included for recall.

candidates.title: Hybrid ideas of artificial intelligence and human: Growth of creativity in college educational programs
candidates.venue: Psychology of Aesthetics, Creativity, and the Arts 20(4), 945-958
candidates.evidence: Title indicates a study of creativity growth from hybrid AI-human ideas in college programs; abstract not accessible, so design and outcomes are unconfirmed. Included for recall.

candidates.title: Symbiosis or stagnation? Investigating the impact of AI on creativity in L1 Chinese writing
candidates.evidence: Title indicates a study of AI effects on creativity in L1 Chinese writing; abstract not accessible to API or search, so design is unconfirmed. Included for recall.

candidates.title: Integrating AIGC into product design ideation teaching: An empirical study on self-efficacy and learning outcomes
candidates.evidence: Empirical field study comparing AIGC-integrated and conventional ideation teaching; AIGC raised self-efficacy, ideation volume, novelty and variety but may have lowered idea quality. Details from search snippet.

candidates.title: Evaluating the impact of AIGC-Supported design ideation on Designers’ cognitive load and creativity
candidates.task: design challenge under three assistance modes
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment in which designers worked with AI support, designer-designer collaboration, or image stimuli; CPSS creativity ratings showed directionally higher novelty and resolution with AI, plus lower cognitive load. Details from search snippet.

candidates.title: Student-AI collaborative creative Problem-Solving: The role of human agency
candidates.evidence: Experiment 1 (170 students) varied independent thinking before or after collaborating with AI; pre-collaboration thinking improved prompts but not final creative output, while deep integration of human ideas with AI output raised creativity. N is Experiment 1 only; details from search snippet.

candidates.title: Human–AI synergy: finding cognitive balance in idea generation for product innovation
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment with 123 product innovators in three conditions (no AI, moderate AI assistance, high AI assistance); moderate assistance produced the most original and feasible ideas, high assistance lowered originality and raised overconfidence (inverted U). Assignment method not stated.

candidates.title: Empowering Engineering Students Through Artificial Intelligence (AI): Blended Human–AI Creative Ideation Processes With ChatGPT
candidates.venue: Computer Applications in Engineering Education 33(1), e22817
candidates.task: engineering student creative ideation with ChatGPT
candidates.evidence: Analyzes whether ChatGPT aids or limits engineering students' creative ideation; a search summary describes a randomized controlled experiment, but random assignment and N were not confirmed from the abstract.

candidates.title: Human-AI Interaction in Creative Tasks: an Experimental Investigation
candidates.venue: Ca' Foscari University of Venice, Department of Economics Working Paper 16/WP/2026
candidates.task: open-ended creative writing in the lab
candidates.evidence: Laboratory experiment randomly assigning participants to access ChatGPT or not; Prolific evaluators scored creative performance, and AI access raised scores only for participants who actively queried the model.

candidates.title: Incentives shape how humans co-create with generative AI
candidates.evidence: Preregistered RCT varying incentives (originality relative to peers vs quality) while all participants could use AI; originality incentives produced collectively more diverse writing and less verbatim use of AI suggestions. N not given on the abstract page.

candidates.title: Personalized AI Scaffolds Synergistic Multi-Turn Collaboration in Creative Work
other_versions: OSF preregistration https://osf.io/qf3g7/ ("CreativityBot: A Personalized AI Assistant to Support Creativity", 2025-01-21; plans a no-AI condition)
candidates.task: marketing campaign for a fictional startup
candidates.evidence: 331 participants randomized to generic, partially personalized or fully personalized LLM assistants; personalized AI produced campaigns of higher rated quality and creativity. AI-variant comparison (no no-AI arm in this report).

candidates.title: Exploration vs. Fixation: Scaffolding Divergent and Convergent Thinking for Human-AI Co-Creation with Generative Models
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects study comparing HAICo, a system with divergent and convergent modes, with ChatGPT for creative image generation; HAICo scored higher on several creativity dimensions. AI-variant comparison.

candidates.title: When AI Sparks Less: Generative AI and The Decline Of Self-Perceived Creativity
candidates.venue: ECIS 2026 Proceedings (European Conference on Information Systems)
candidates.task: creative task with or without GenAI
candidates.evidence: Experiment with 82 participants found GenAI use lowered intrinsic task motivation, domain-relevant skills and creativity-relevant skills while self-evaluated performance was unchanged. Outcomes may be self-reported; included for recall.

candidates.title: Effects of generative artificial intelligence on higher-order thinking skills and artificial intelligence literacy in nursing undergraduates: A quasi-experimental study
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experiment in which 132 nursing students were described as randomly divided into GenAI and control groups (66 each); creativity and creative thinking scores rose more in the GenAI group. Measures may be self-report scales; details from a search snippet.

candidates.title: Sketching with generative AI: verbal but not visual inspiration mitigates cognitive fixations
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Cognitive Science Society 47
candidates.task: sketching abstract concepts before and after GPT-4 inspiration
candidates.evidence: Participants sketched abstract concepts before and after GPT-4 verbal or visual inspiration; verbal inspiration raised semantic distance and uniqueness of sketches, visual inspiration did not. Human and GPT-4 creativity scoring. Related OSF project https://osf.io/v637p/.

candidates.title: More explanation, less exploration: Semantic anchoring in generative AI-assisted ideation
candidates.venue: OSF (data and analysis code for a manuscript)
candidates.evidence: OSF project with data and code for a manuscript on semantic anchoring in GenAI-assisted ideation; the manuscript itself was not located, so design and N are unknown. Included as an early signal.

candidates.title: Replication Report on “An empirical investigation of the impact of ChatGPT on creativity”
candidates.task: reanalysis of Lee and Chung (2024) experiments
candidates.evidence: Notebook with Stata code that reproduces and runs robustness checks on Lee and Chung (2024), an RCT on ChatGPT and creativity already in the collection. Reanalysis, not a new experiment.

candidates.title: When ChatGPT Writes Your Research Proposal: Scientific Creativity in the Age of Generative AI
candidates.task: research proposal (hypothesis and experiment design) writing
candidates.evidence: Blinded expert ratings compared ChatGPT-4 research proposals with graduate students' proposals; ChatGPT scored higher overall and on originality and meaningfulness.

candidates.title: GenAI Creativity in Narrative Tasks: Exploring New Forms of Creativity
candidates.evidence: Benchmarked ChatGPT against human performance on standardized creativity tests; high fluency but average creative output.

candidates.title: The paradox of creativity in generative AI: high performance, human-like bias, and limited differential evaluation
other_versions: OSF record "Generative AI vs Human Creativity: Divergent Thinking and Fixation Bias" (2025-07-21)
candidates.evidence: ChatGPT-4o did the egg task and was compared with 47 human participants and data from eight prior studies; ChatGPT was more productive but showed similar fixation and poor discrimination of original ideas.

candidates.title: Beyond the brush: Human versus artificial intelligence creativity in the realm of generative art
candidates.authors: Seli, Ragnhildstveit, Orwig, Bellaiche, Spooner, Barr
candidates.venue: Psychology of Aesthetics, Creativity, and the Arts 20(4), 984-992
candidates.evidence: DALL-E 3 images from prompts by professional artists, novice artists and ChatGPT-4 were rated for creativity by 299 participants; professional-artist prompts were most creative, then AI prompts, then novices. N counts raters.

candidates.title: Stable Diffusion Models Reveal a Persisting Human–AI Gap in Visual Creativity
other_versions: OSF data record "Stable diffusion models reveal a persisting human–AI gap in visual creativity" (Martín, Cerda-Company)
candidates.evidence: Compared images by visual artists, non-artists and Stable Diffusion under high or low human guidance; human raters (N = 255) and GPT-4o rated creativity, with artists > non-artists >= human-guided AI > self-guided AI. N counts raters.

candidates.title: Divergent creativity in humans and large language models
candidates.task: Divergent Association Task and creative writing
candidates.evidence: Compared semantic divergence of LLM outputs with 100,000 humans on the DAT and haiku, synopsis and flash-fiction tasks; LLMs beat the average human on the DAT but stayed below more creative humans.

candidates.title: Echoes in AI: Quantifying lack of plot diversity in LLM outputs
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 122(35), e2504966122
candidates.evidence: Introduced the Sui Generis score; GPT-4 and LLaMA-3 stories repeat plot elements across generations while plots of human-written stories are rarely echoed, i.e., lower plot diversity for LLMs.

candidates.title: How funny is ChatGPT? A comparison of human- and A.I.-produced jokes
candidates.evidence: ChatGPT-3.5 and laypeople answered the same comedic prompts, and ChatGPT headlines were compared with The Onion; raters found ChatGPT humor equally or more funny.

candidates.title: How humorous is AI? Exploring ChatGPT's role in humor generation and human-AI interaction
candidates.evidence: Compared GPT-4o humor with human-generated humor; GPT-4o outperformed humans on text-based but not image-based humor. Details from search snippet.

candidates.title: The originality of machines: AI takes the Torrance Test
candidates.evidence: GPT-4 (ChatGPT) took the TTCT and was compared with human samples and national norms; it scored in the top 1% for originality and fluency.

candidates.title: Is artificial intelligence more creative than humans?
candidates.evidence: Administered the DAT to GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 and compared with a large human baseline; both scored above the human mean.

candidates.title: Does human–AI collaboration lead to more creative art? Aesthetic evaluation of human-made and AI-generated haiku poetry
candidates.evidence: Aesthetic and creativity evaluations of human-made haiku, AI-generated haiku and human-AI collaborative haiku. Abstract not accessible to the API; design from title.

candidates.title: The fluency-based semantic network of LLMs differs from humans
candidates.authors: Wang, Deng, Wang, Li, Xiao, Zhang
candidates.venue: Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humans 3, 100103
candidates.evidence: Compared semantic networks from human and LLM (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, LLaMA) fluency responses; LLM networks were less interconnected and less flexible. Included for recall as a flexibility comparison.

candidates.title: Diminished diversity-of-thought in a standard large language model
candidates.task: Many Labs 2 replication items answered by GPT-3.5
candidates.evidence: GPT-3.5 answers showed near-zero variation ("correct answer" effect) compared with human samples, which the authors link to diminished diversity of thought. Not a creativity task; included for recall on homogeneity.

candidates.title: Who Holds the Creative Edge? Human or AI
candidates.evidence: Compared human participants with LLMs prompted to impersonate each participant on AUT, TTCT and RAT.

candidates.title: The creative performance of the AI agents ChatGPT and Google Magenta compared to human-based solutions in a standardized melody continuation task
candidates.evidence: Compared melody continuations by ChatGPT and Google Magenta with human-based solutions on creative performance.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence and the creative process: Does AI-creativity extend beyond divergent thinking?
candidates.task: Future Problem Solving World Solutions Challenge
candidates.evidence: Three GPT-4o entries were blind-scored against 68 student team entries; AI scored in the top 15% on all measures but did not differ from students on creative strength.

candidates.title: Has the creativity of large-language models peaked?
candidates.evidence: Evaluated 14 LLMs on the DAT and AUT against human benchmarks; models beat the average human on the AUT but only 0.28% of responses reached the human top 10%, with large intra-model variability.

candidates.title: Exploring Creative Inflection Points: A Comparative Study of Human and GenAI Design Task Performance
candidates.evidence: Compared creative inflection points in human and GenAI design task performance across three design challenges.

candidates.title: Human versus artificial creativity: A case study in poetry
candidates.evidence: Case study (1 poet, 1 poem) in which two expert poets compared a human poem with an LLM poem written from the same prompt. Very small comparison; included for recall.

candidates.title: Automating psychological hypothesis generation with AI: when large language models meet causal graph
candidates.evidence: Hypotheses generated by an LLM plus causal graph were compared with doctoral students' research ideas on novelty and related ratings.

candidates.title: Machine-assisted social psychology hypothesis generation
candidates.evidence: Experts rated model-generated and human-generated social psychology hypotheses on clarity, originality and impact.

candidates.title: Transmission Versus Truth, Imitation Versus Innovation: What Children Can Do That Large Language and Language-and-Vision Models Cannot (Yet)
candidates.task: tool innovation and causal discovery tasks
candidates.evidence: Contrasted LLM and vision-language model responses with children on designing new tools and discovering causal structures (innovation). Included for recall; not a rated-creativity outcome.

candidates.title: Artificial intelligence and its impact on creativity and diversity: An empirical study of large language model-generated product ideas
candidates.authors: Terwiesch, Meincke, Girotra, Mollick, Nave, Ulrich
candidates.task: new product ideas for college students
candidates.evidence: LLM-generated product ideas had higher average quality than human ideas but were less novel and less diverse as a set; tested prompting and pooling methods that restore diversity. Published version of the collected SSRN paper 4526071 ("Ideas Are Dimes a Dozen").

candidates.title: Characterising the Creative Process in Humans and Large Language Models
candidates.task: Alternate Uses Task and verbal fluency
candidates.evidence: Compared how humans and LLMs move through semantic space on the AUT (persistent vs flexible paths) and how this relates to creativity scores.

candidates.title: ChatGPT as an inventor: eliciting the strengths and weaknesses of current large language models against humans in engineering design
candidates.venue: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering Design, Analysis and Manufacturing 39, e6
candidates.evidence: ChatGPT-4 directed a team as an autonomous designer and was compared with graduate engineering student teams; strong concept generation but design fixation.

candidates.title: Expertise Elevates AI Usage: Experimental Evidence Comparing Laypeople and Professional Artists
candidates.authors: Eisenmann, Karjus, Canet Sola, Brinkmann, Supriyatno, Rahwan
candidates.task: text-to-image copying and creative image creation
candidates.evidence: Preregistered comparison of 50 professional artists and matched laypeople using a text-to-image tool; artists produced more divergent images, and GPT-4o did slightly better than artists on average. Expertise comparison, no no-AI arm.

candidates.title: Using AI to Generate Visual Art: Do Individual Differences in Creativity Predict AI-Assisted Art Quality?
candidates.task: word sets for an AI art generator (DALL-E)
candidates.evidence: Individual differences in divergent thinking (DAT, AUT) predicted rated creativity of AI-assisted images made from participants' word sets. No no-AI comparison; included for recall.

candidates.title: Large language models are homogeneously creative
candidates.evidence: Compared population-level response diversity of many LLMs with humans; LLM responses resemble each other far more than human responses do. Published version of the collected arXiv paper 2501.19361 ("We're Different, We're the Same").

candidates.title: Uncovering the effect of Gen AI-assisted learning on students’ creativity: A meta-analysis from quasi-experimental evidence
candidates.evidence: Meta-analysis of 32 quasi-experimental studies; GenAI-assisted learning had a moderate positive effect on students' creativity (g = 0.420). Details from search snippet.

candidates.title: Students’ writing skills and creativity in the age of artificial intelligence: A systematic review of creativity across diverse AI-supported writing contexts
candidates.evidence: Systematic review of creativity in AI-supported writing contexts. Abstract not accessible to the API.

candidates.title: Does Generative Artificial Intelligence Improve Students’ Higher-Order Thinking? A Meta-Analysis Based on 29 Experiments and Quasi-Experiments
candidates.evidence: Meta-analysis of 29 experiments and quasi-experiments; GenAI had a moderate positive effect on higher-order thinking but a relatively limited effect on creativity.

candidates.title: Differentiated Empowerment and Boundary Effects of AI-Assisted Music Learning: A Mixed-Methods Study of Learning Motivation, Self-Regulated Learning, and Creative Performance
candidates.task: three-level meta-analysis of AI-assisted music learning
candidates.evidence: Mixed-methods review with a three-level meta-analysis; creative performance g = 1.21 with high heterogeneity. AI roles include evaluative feedback and generative support, not only GenAI.

candidates.title: The role of generative AI in facilitating children's creative thinking and cognitive development: a systematic scoping review
candidates.task: scoping review of children's creative thinking
candidates.evidence: Scoping review of 24 sources (22 primary studies) on GenAI and children's creative thinking; possible benefits for divergent thinking and narrative creativity, weak designs.

candidates.title: The impact of AI-based painting technology on children’s creative thinking
candidates.task: systematic review of AI painting tools for children
candidates.evidence: PRISMA review of 20 empirical studies on AI painting tools and children's creative thinking; notes enhanced expression but risk of cognitive homogenization.

candidates.title: Exploring the effect of GenAI on learning outcomes in higher education: a three-level meta-analysis
candidates.task: three-level meta-analysis of GenAI learning outcomes
candidates.evidence: Meta-analysis of 36 studies (132 effect sizes) on GenAI in higher education; a combined understanding, cognitive and creative outcomes category had g = 0.669. Not creativity-specific; included for recall.

candidates.title: Generative AI for Creative Learning in K-12 Education: Insights from a Systematic Scoping Review
other_versions: PsyArXiv 10.31234/osf.io/npd9f_v1 ("Generative Artificial Intelligence and Creativity in K–12 Education: A Systematic Scoping Review")
candidates.task: scoping review of GenAI and creativity in K-12
candidates.evidence: Systematic scoping review of 45 studies (2017-2025) on GenAI for creative learning in K-12: assessment, co-creativity, perceptions, enhancement.

candidates.title: How Does Artificial Intelligence Shape Creative Thinking Processes in Educational Contexts? A Systematic Review of Cognitive Mechanisms
candidates.evidence: PRISMA review of 49 empirical studies (2022-2025) on AI-integrated creative thinking processes in education; the same AI use showed facilitative and inhibitory mechanisms.

candidates.title: The cognitive impact of ChatGPT in higher education: A systematic review of critical and creative thinking outcomes
candidates.task: systematic review of ChatGPT and creative thinking
candidates.evidence: Systematic review of critical and creative thinking outcomes of ChatGPT in higher education. Abstract not accessible to the API.

candidates.title: AI vs humans in the AUT: Simulations to LLMs
candidates.task: review of AI vs human AUT studies
candidates.evidence: Narrative review of studies applying creative machines and LLMs to the AUT; LLMs perform near or above human levels on originality and usefulness.

candidates.title: Narrowed creativity: a systematic review and meta-analysis of generative AI collaboration and learning outcomes in art and design education
candidates.task: meta-analysis of GenAI in art and design education
candidates.evidence: OSF project for a systematic review and meta-analysis that estimates both mean effects (Hedges g) and dispersion of creative outcomes (lnVR, lnCVR) to test whether GenAI narrows student output. Results not located.

candidates.title: The Hollowing Out of Local News: A Longitudinal Study of Journalistic Performance Decline and Content Homogenisation at a Major UK Publisher
candidates.evidence: Panel of 27 Reach plc newspapers shows rising content homogenisation; the rise coincides with a national content hub and AI-assisted editorial tools, but AI is not isolated as a cause. Included for recall.
